text:
leo (eng): hey @people-ops — urgent: I was seen at an urgent care in Lisbon on 2026-05-03. I lost my physical ID card while traveling and the clinic says they couldn't verify coverage and billed me as self-pay. EOB just came in showing patient responsibility $180. I'm on the International Core plan. claim# 77665544. member id ends 0142. any fast help?

maya (People Ops): sorry that happened — can you DM a photo of the receipt and the clinic invoice? Also do you have the clinic name and any provider NPI? If you signed in with an email, that sometimes helps.

leo (eng): clinic is QuickCare Lisboa, no NPI on receipt, they put "unknown insurance" on the form. I have a scanned receipt and the payment confirmation from the clinic (I paid on-site). attaching in DM.

sami (Benefits): we can file a retroactive eligibility verification and a reimbursement request. Two tracks: 1) ask carrier to reprocess the claim as in-network for the service date if member was active (we'll need proof of membership effective date and the receipt), 2) file for a direct reimbursement from the carrier for the out-of-pocket if they find the claim was eligible.

leo (eng): my plan effective date is 2026-02-01. I can upload passport entry stamp + boarding pass and the payment receipt.

maya (People Ops): please upload in the claims portal: EOB (if carrier sent one), receipt, proof of travel (boarding pass) and a signed HIPAA release so benefits team can call on your behalf: https://benefits.example.com/claims-portal. If you want immediate help, we can also advance the payment under Redwood's emergency travel assistance policy — you would repay only if carrier denies.

sami (Benefits): opened carrier inquiry REF-LIS-2026-334. Requested retroactive eligibility check for service date 2026-05-03 and asked carrier to consider the claim under international urgent care network rules. Also requested any available in-network partner match in Lisbon.

claims-bot: Carrier SLA: initial response within 8 business days. Case REF-LIS-2026-334 created.

maya (People Ops): @leo if you want the company to advance funds now, DM me a copy of the receipt + bank details and I'll route to Payroll Ops. Policy note: emergency advance capped at $250 and requires sign-off from People Ops director.

leo (eng): thanks — going to upload docs and DM you. Appreciate the speedy help.

sami (Benefits): FYI common reason for OOP in foreign urgent care: front-desk couldn't validate subscriber without card and keyed a temporary patient id triggering out-of-network processing. Carrier often will reprocess once we show the member was active on that date. We'll attach boarding pass + plan effective pdf.

hr-bot: Travel claims FAQ & upload: https://benefits.example.com/international-claims. For emergency advances: submit here: https://payments.example.com/advances and tag People Ops.

maya (People Ops): once docs are uploaded I'll send carrier the signed release and ask for expedited handling because it's an emergency travel claim. I'll update thread when we hear back. :white_check_mark:
